## The reconstruction framework (`dynamics/reconstruct`) {#sec-ch04-framework}

### Summary

A Riemann solver needs two states on each face, one from each side, but the code stores only one average per
cell. The reconstruction makes the two face states from the cell averages around the face. snapy keeps one
reconstruction for the vertical direction and one shared by the two horizontal directions, because the vertical
carries the background stratification and usually wants a different scheme. Inside each, density and tracers
take the interpolant the deck names, while velocity and pressure take a linear partner when that name is a
WENO type. The framework is always on; with no `reconstruct` block a deck gets donor cell with `shock`[^rg-d442901d55b4] on.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Builds $q^{\mathrm L}_f$[^rg-2671c43c7524] and $q^{\mathrm R}_f$ on every face of one direction from cell values, @eq-ch04-framework-map.

**Data.** Reads $\mathbf W$[^rg-99fd7d49b37f] with ghosts; writes a $[2, N_{\mathrm{var}}, \ldots]$ array of left and right face states.

**Placement.** Every RK stage, in `HydroImpl::forward`, before the Riemann solver of each direction.

**Activation.** `dynamics/reconstruct/{vertical,horizontal}/{type,scale,shock}`; with that sub-block `dc`, false, false; without, `shock` true.

**Guarantee / limits.** The order of the interpolant; uniform-grid weights; floors from the equation of state.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch04-framework-tests; `test_plm.release`, the probe run, `recon_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C7]`.
:::

Local symbols: $q^{\mathrm L}_f, q^{\mathrm R}_f$ the left and right states of face $f$
(appendix A, notation group 4); $\mathcal W$ the reconstruction operator (appendix A, notation group 4); $f = i - \tfrac12$ the face below cell $i$
in the code's face numbering; $n_{\mathrm s}$ the stencil width of an interpolant (`stencils()`, count);
$N_{\mathrm{var}}$ the number of rows of $\mathbf W$ (count).

### Derivation

#### Which cell value lands on which face

The face numbering is the part a reader of the code gets wrong most often. Fix one direction and number the
cells $0..n-1$ along it, ghosts included; face $f$ is the face between cells $f-1$ and $f$.

1. *An interpolant returns two values per cell.* `left` gives the value at the lower face of each cell it can
   reach, $\mathcal W[q]_{i-1/2}^{+}$, and `right` the value at its upper face, $\mathcal W[q]_{i+1/2}^{-}$. With a
   stencil of $n_{\mathrm s}$ cells the first reachable cell is $(n_{\mathrm s}-1)/2$ and the output has
   $n - n_{\mathrm s} + 1$ entries (`vec[dim] -= stencils() - 1`).
2. *The lower-face value of cell $i$ is the right state of face $i$.* Seen from face $i$, cell $i$ is on its
   right. `_apply_inplace` writes `left` into `wlr[IRT]` starting at index `il - 1`.
3. *The upper-face value of cell $i$ is the left state of face $i+1$.* Cell $i$ is on the left of face $i+1$, so
   `right` goes into `wlr[ILT]` starting one index later, at `il`.
4. *Hence*

   $$
   q^{\mathrm R}_{i} = \mathcal W[q]_{i-1/2}^{+},\qquad q^{\mathrm L}_{i+1} = \mathcal W[q]_{i+1/2}^{-},
   $$ {#eq-ch04-framework-map}

   with the two output slices offset by one. Faces outside the computed range are filled by copying the nearest
   computed face, not by running the interpolant on ghost data. In the code, @eq-ch04-framework-map is `_apply_inplace` ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp _apply_inplace >}}).

#### How many ghost cells, and why the run fails rather than reads garbage

A ghost zone is the slab of ghost cells on each side of a block, in every direction with more than one cell;
`nghost`[^rg-0d1aafefcc3b] is the number of cells across it, one value for the block (its default and setup guards are in
@sec-ch12-yaml). The width an interpolant needs, and the guard that enforces it, are these:

1. *The ghost width.* `forward` sets `nghost = stencils() / 2 + 1`, so $n_{\mathrm s} = 1, 3, 5$ give 1, 2, 3.
   Per scheme: donor cell `dc` ($n_{\mathrm s}=1$) needs 1; `plm`, `cp3` and `weno3` ($n_{\mathrm s}=3$) need 2;
   `cp5` and `weno5` ($n_{\mathrm s}=5$) need 3. `ppm` also reads five cells, but its first stage throws
   (@sec-ch04-ppm).
2. *The interior range.* `il = nghost` and `iu = n - nghost`.
3. *The guard.* `TORCH_CHECK(il <= iu)` refuses a block too thin for the stencil, so no face value is ever built
   from a stencil that leaves the array.

#### Which rows take which interpolant

The code is the only record of the split; no source states a reason for it.

1. *Two interpolants per reconstruction.* `reset` builds `pinterp1` and `pinterp2` from the same options, named
   `interp1` and `interp2`.
2. *The names select the partner.* `InterpImpl::create` returns the named type for both, except that for
   `weno3` and `weno5` it returns `Center3Interp` and `Center5Interp` when the module name ends in `2`.
3. *The rows.* With `shock: false`, `forward` reconstructs the density row with `pinterp1`, the velocity and
   pressure rows with `pinterp2`, and the species rows with `pinterp1`.
4. *Hence under `weno5` velocity and pressure are fifth-order linear and unlimited*, while density and tracers
   are limited. With `shock: true` every row goes through `pinterp1` in one call; with the equation of state's
   `limiter`[^rg-e5bc5308fcd8] on its species rows are then clamped at zero, and density and pressure are not floored. The probe
   below does not cover that clamp; `test_species_face_clamp` does (@sec-ch08-reconfloors).

(b) The row split with shock false: density and tracers take interp1 (green), velocity and pressure take interp2 (blue). With shock true every row takes interp1."
#| fig-alt: "Left: a row of six cells, the outer two hatched, with two orange triangles marking the first and last face read. Right: four row names with arrows to either interp1 or interp2."

**Floors.** They come from the equation of state, not from the reconstruct options (@sec-ch08-reconfloors).
With the equation of state's `limiter` on and the caller's `floor` argument true, the density row is clamped to
`density_floor` and the pressure row to `pressure_floor`; the species rows are clamped at zero whenever the
limiter is on, whatever `floor` says. The well-balanced $x_1$ path calls `forward` with `floor = false`, because
it reconstructs perturbations that may be negative (@sec-ch05-wbx1). The `shock: true` branch clamps the species
rows at zero when the limiter is on and returns before the density and pressure floors. The passive-scalar
reconstruction, which has no hydro parent, clamps every row at zero whatever the limiter (@sec-ch08-reconfloors).

**Order.** The framework adds no error of its own: the face value has the order of the interpolant
(@sec-ch04-dc to @sec-ch04-weno), measured on a uniform grid. On a stretched $x_1$ grid the same uniform weights
are applied, and the design order is not reached.

### Code

**The shipped block.** The shipped decks name both blocks in full:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `vertical`[^rg-c00856b883f2], `type`[^rg-e7755bb7941e], `horizontal`[^rg-ae7031b3a70c].
```yaml
dynamics:
  reconstruct:
    vertical:   {type: weno5, scale: false, shock: false}
    horizontal: {type: weno5, scale: false, shock: false}
```

{{< include 04-spatial-discretization/_howto.qmd >}}

{{< include 04-spatial-discretization/_howto-native.qmd >}}

**What the parser accepts and refuses.** `ReconstructOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}) and the factory apply, in
order:

1. *`reconstruct` takes only `vertical` and `horizontal`*; any other key is refused by `check_keys`.
2. *Each block takes only `shock`, `type` and `scale`*; `limiter` or a floor key is refused ("unknown key
   'dynamics/reconstruct/vertical/limiter'. Valid keys: shock, type, scale"), because the floors are the
   equation of state's.
3. *An unknown `type` is refused* by `InterpImpl::create` ("Interp: unknown type bp3"): only `dc`, `plm`, `ppm`,
   `cp3`, `cp5`, `weno3`, `weno5` are registered.
4. *`ppm` is accepted and then throws* on the first stage ("PPM interpolation is not implemented yet.";
   @sec-ch04-ppm).
5. *Defaults depend on whether the block exists.* With the block present, a missing `type`, `scale` or `shock`
   is `dc`, `false`, `false`. With no `reconstruct` block, or no `vertical`/`horizontal` key, the options object
   is used as constructed: `dc`, `scale` false and **`shock` true**, because `ReconstructOptionsImpl` declares
   `shock = true`.

A probe against the pin build confirms items 2 to 5.[^fw4-probe]

**The excerpt.** The row split of `ReconstructImpl::forward`
({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
  if (options->shock()) {
    _apply_inplace(dim, il, iu, w, pinterp1, result);
    ...
    if (phydro->options->eos()->limiter() && nvar > ICY) {
      result.narrow(1, ICY, nvar - ICY).clamp_min_(0.);
    }
    return result;
  }
  ...
  // density
  _apply_inplace(dim, il, iu, w.narrow(0, IDN, 1), pinterp1,
                 result.narrow(1, IDN, 1));
  ...
  // velocity/pressure
  int len = std::min((int)IPR, nvar - 1);
  _apply_inplace(dim, il, iu, w.narrow(0, IVX, len), pinterp2,
                 result.narrow(1, IVX, len));
  ...
  // others
  _apply_inplace(dim, il, iu, w.narrow(0, ICY, ny), pinterp1,
                 result.narrow(1, ICY, ny));
```

The `shock` branch is step 4 of the row split; the three calls below it are step 3; each `_apply_inplace` is
@eq-ch04-framework-map for its rows.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |

| no block: the constructed options | {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=1 >}} | `from_yaml` | `shock` true |
| face index map | {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp _apply_inplace >}} | `_apply_inplace` | |

| which interpolant is `interp2` | {{< code src/recon/interpolation.cpp InterpImpl::create >}} | `Center5Interp` | `weno3`, `weno5` |

### Tests

The `ch04-framework` record in `tools/do-cards.yaml` runs the six-step scheme card and then its `run.check`
float32 test through the N8 runner (`tools/tests/test_do_cards_run.py`): the prototype keeps the input dtype and
matches the built-in `dc` reconstruction exactly in float32 too.

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_plm.release` | a constant field is reconstructed exactly by `dc`, `plm` and `weno5` in all three directions | `allclose` defaults | `torch::allclose` |
| the probe run (this report) | the parser refusals and the two sets of defaults of the Code layer | exact (throws or constructs) | a parser contract |
| `recon_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C7]` (this report) | the interpolant weights and their measured orders | symbolic; fitted orders | stated in the check |
| `derivation_check.py` `[C4]`–`[C6]` (this report) | the weights re-derived equal the coefficient buffers | exact | sympy |

: Tests of the reconstruction framework. {#tbl-ch04-framework-tests}

`test_plm.release` passes at the pin (@tbl-ch04-ctest-run). The probe constructs a block for each case of the
Code layer and runs one stage. No test asserts the row split itself: a swap of `interp1` and `interp2` would be
caught only by an accuracy test.

### Limits

1. **Two sets of defaults.** A deck without a `reconstruct` block runs with `shock` on, one that names the block
   but not `shock` runs with it off. The two differ in which rows are limited and whether floors apply.
2. **Uniform-grid weights.** Every interpolant uses fixed rational weights for equal cell widths; on a stretched
   $x_1$ grid the design order is not reached and no warning is printed.
3. **Dead option members.** `ReconstructOptionsImpl` carries `density_floor`, `pressure_floor`, `limiter`,
   `is_boundary_lower` and `is_boundary_upper`; `forward` reads none of them, and `report` prints them.
4. **A disabled branch.** A block inside a comment in `forward` would narrow the range next to a physical
   boundary before reconstructing velocity and pressure. It is not compiled.
5. **`scale`.** What the key does is derived in @sec-ch04-weno; for `dc`, `plm`, `cp3` and `cp5` it is read and
   has no effect.
